1Purpose

This policy is the frame for the module at [Provider name]. It names the seven standards we work to and the policy that carries each one, the roles that run the module, and the rules that apply across the whole module. It sets no time limit and restates no commitment of its own: each of POL-ECS-02 to POL-ECS-08 holds its commitments, its clocks and its checks in one place. It is for families, our workers, the other services in a child's team, and the people who check our work.

2Applies to

  • Every child who receives early childhood supports from us, and their , from first contact until supports end.
  • Everyone who works for [Provider name] and has contact with those children or families: employees, contractors, students, volunteers and key personnel.
  • Every place we work: the family home, early learning and school settings, community places, our premises, and phone or video sessions.
  • A sole trader or partnership registered for these supports, in the same way as a larger provider.

This policy is the shared frame for the module. POL-ECS-02 to POL-ECS-08 each set out one standard in full, with its own commitments, times and checks; nothing in this policy changes them. POL-CHS-01 Child Safe Policy sets the child safety rules for all our work with children; until it is written, the appendix to POL-ECS-02 holds the state and territory reporting schedule.

3Commitments

C1

We will do what POL-ECS-02 The Child Policy (Early Childhood Supports) commits to (the child, s 56).

C2

We will do what POL-ECS-03 The Family Policy (Early Childhood Supports) commits to (the family, s 57).

C3

We will do what POL-ECS-04 Inclusion Policy (Early Childhood Supports) commits to (inclusion, s 58).

C4

We will do what POL-ECS-05 Collaboration Policy (Early Childhood Supports) commits to (collaboration, s 59).

C5

We will do what POL-ECS-06 Capacity Building Policy (Early Childhood Supports) commits to (capacity building, s 60).

C6

We will do what POL-ECS-07 Evidence-Informed Practice Policy (Early Childhood Supports) commits to (evidence-informed supports, s 61).

C7

We will do what POL-ECS-08 Outcome Based Approach Policy (Early Childhood Supports) commits to (outcome based approach, s 62).

4Ground rules

G1

A child's safety comes before everything else in this policy. A worker who is worried about a child acts on that worry first.

G2

A person with decides about the child's supports. We ask for the child's own views in a way that fits their age and how they communicate, and we record them.

G3

One route for every concern. A practice concern goes to the . A conduct or safety concern about a colleague or a manager goes to the Chief Executive. A concern about the Chief Executive or an owner goes to the chair of the governing body, or in a sole trader's business to the independent contact named in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register. A child who may be at goes to the the same day, under PRO-ECS-02 The Child Procedure (Early Childhood Supports). The person a concern is about never handles it.

G4

The time limits of the module are set in POL-ECS-02 to POL-ECS-08 and the procedures under them; the Module clocks table at the end of these ground rules reproduces them, and this policy sets none of its own. Where the law sets a shorter time, the shorter time applies.

G5

The appendix to POL-ECS-02 holds the state and territory reporting schedule: the law of [state or territory] on who must report, the test, where, how fast, and the duty of every adult to tell police of child sexual abuse. POL-CHS-01, when written, holds the wider child safe standards and reportable conduct rules. The Quality Manager checks the schedule every 12 months and when the law changes.

G6

Each fact is held once. REG-ECS-01 Early Childhood Supports Register is the one register for the module and holds dates, names, counts and record numbers. The forms hold the detail and the family's words.

G7

A family can say no to a , a referral, a team meeting or a question. Saying no is recorded and is never a reason to reduce supports.

G8

A complaint made by a child or family at any point is handled under PRO-FBK-01 Feedback and Complaints Management Procedure. A child's "stop" or "not happy" signal is a complaint the child can make in their own way.

G9

A sole trader holds every role except practice supervisor and independent contact for concerns. An outside practice supervisor with early childhood experience and the independent contact named in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register are the checks on the sole trader's own work.

G10

The is the practitioner accountable for the child's plan and the register row. Where the family chooses a key worker from our team, the key worker is the plan lead, and when the key worker changes the plan-lead role moves with it the same day.

9Words we use

345 words
early childhood supports
supports for a young child with developmental delay or disability, and their family, under the registration class "early intervention supports for early childhood".
family
the parents, carers and other people who raise the child, as the family itself describes them.
parental responsibility
the legal authority to make decisions for a child. A court or child protection order can change who holds it.
support network
the relatives, friends, educators and others in the child's everyday life whom the family chooses to involve.
everyday routines
the things the child does most days, such as meals, play, bath time, getting dressed and going to early learning.
key worker
the one practitioner the family chooses as their main contact. Where the family chooses a key worker, that person is the plan lead.
team around the child
the family, our practitioners and the other providers who work together on the child's plan.
plan lead
the practitioner accountable for the child's plan and the register row.
practice supervisor
the clinical supervisor of the early childhood practitioners.
practitioner drafting for the plan lead
the practitioner the plan lead asks to draft the plan under PRO-ECS-08. The plan lead stays accountable for the plan.
functional outcome
something the child will do in daily life, written so the family can see when it has happened.
coaching
helping a parent, carer or educator practise a strategy in their own routine, in place of doing it for them.
both clearances
an NDIS worker screening clearance, and the working with children check of [state or territory].
child safety lead
the role the Chief Executive names to receive every concern about a child and to see that reports are made.
risk of harm
the words this module uses for the reporting threshold. Our test is that you suspect on reasonable grounds that a child is at risk of harm. The appendix to POL-ECS-02 gives the exact term used in [state or territory].
business day
a day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday in the state or territory where the participant lives.

1Purpose

The result: every is supported in a way from their first day. Every practitioner starts from what the family knows and wants at every contact. A family that has a has one first call, who keeps the family's priorities in front of the team.

This procedure gives effect to POL-ECS-03 The Family Policy (Early Childhood Supports), C1, C3, C5, C6, C7, C8, C9, C12 and C13.

2When and who

Start this procedure when:

  • a family accepts our offer of (steps 1 to 4)
  • any practitioner has a contact with the family: a session, a call, a message or a meeting (steps 5 to 13)
  • the family has chosen a key worker, has chosen none, or wants to change (steps 14 to 20)
  • the family says no, asks for a change, sees something differently, or is unhappy (steps 21 to 24 and Decision table 1)
  • a plan review is due (step 25).

Who acts:

  • The Service Manager names the and a backup.
  • The plan lead opens the child's row, explains how we work, and is the family's first call where the family chose no key worker.
  • The key worker is the one practitioner the family chose as their main contact. The key worker may be ours or from another service. Where the key worker is ours, they are the plan lead.
  • Every practitioner works the family-centred way at every contact.
  • The Quality Manager samples contact records every 3 months.

In a small provider the Service Manager and the plan lead are one person. A sole trader holds every role, and is the key worker if the family chooses them. A sole trader asks the independent contact named in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register to read a sample of 3 every 6 months.

3Before you start

  • The family has accepted our offer and the intake is done (FRM-SUP-01 Referral and Intake Form).
  • The family has a record, FRM-ECS-02 Family Strengths, Needs and Priorities Record, or will have one under PRO-ECS-03 The Family Procedure (Early Childhood Supports).
  • The offer of a key worker and the family's choice are made under PRO-ECS-05 Collaboration Procedure (Early Childhood Supports). They are recorded in Section D of FRM-ECS-04 Team Around the Child Record. This procedure starts from that choice.
  • The child's safety controls line is agreed under PRO-ECS-02 The Child Procedure (Early Childhood Supports) step 2. The first session does not go ahead while column I of REG-ECS-01 Early Childhood Supports Register is empty for the type of setting it is in. That is the only pre-session gate.

4Watch out

  • Telling before asking makes the practitioner the only expert. The family's knowledge is lost, and the family stops speaking up. Ask first.
  • A strategy that does not fit the family's week will not be used. The family is blamed, and the child gets no benefit. Work inside their .
  • "Do you understand?" gets a yes whatever the truth. The family leaves unsure what to do. Ask them to say or show it back.
  • A family's no is a choice. Reducing a support because of a no punishes the child. It can breach the duty to respect self-determination and decision-making (Code of Conduct Rules, s 6(1)(a)).
  • A child's safety comes before a family's choice. If you think a child may be at , tell the the same day. A delay can leave a child in danger.
  • A child or a brother or sister who interprets can change what is said. The meaning is lost, and a child carries an adult's worries.

5Steps

Start with a new family

Step 1

The Service Manager

Name the plan lead and a backup for the child.

Choose a practitioner who can meet the family where they want. They must have and children's rights training, shown in REG-HRM-01 Worker Screening Register and REG-HRM-02 Training and Competency Register. Tell the family who it is, how to reach them and who the backup is. The family can ask for someone else. Enter both at FRM-ECS-04 question 3. Where the family later chooses a key worker from our team, that person becomes the plan lead (step 18).

Result
The family knows one named person of ours and the backup.
Record
REG-ECS-01 col D; FRM-ECS-04 Q3
Time limit
The day the family accepts our offer (our standard)

Written on: Register, Row opened and plan leadRegister col D

Step 2

The plan lead

Open the child's row in REG-ECS-01.

Use one row for each child. Brothers and sisters each have their own row, linked in column AF. Write the record number in column A. Write your name, role and the time in column D. Put the row number on FRM-ECS-02 question 1.

Result
The child has one record number that follows them through every early childhood record.
Record
REG-ECS-01 col A
Time limit
Within 2 of the family accepting our offer (our standard)

Written on: Register, Record numberRegister col A

Step 3

The plan lead

Fill the family columns in REG-ECS-01 from what the family has already told us.

Use FRM-SUP-01 questions 7 and 8 and the documents the family gave at intake (REG-SUP-01 Participant and Service Agreement Register, when written, will hold intake and the service agreement). Enter the people in column E, the language and how the child communicates in column G, and who holds , on what basis and with any order reference, in column F. Write "not yet asked", with the date, for anything missing. Columns I and J are filled under PRO-ECS-02.

Result
The first session starts from what we know, and nobody asks the family the same question twice.
Record
REG-ECS-01 col E; REG-ECS-01 col F; REG-ECS-01 col G

Before the first session (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-03, commitment 6POL-ECS-03 C6Written on: Register, Family and support networkRegister col ERegister, Language, communication and cultureRegister col G

Step 4

The plan lead

Explain to the family how we work.

Use the family's language and way. Say that the family leads and decides, and that we ask before we tell. Say the family can say no, skip any question and change their mind. Say a no never reduces a support. Say who their one contact is, and how to give feedback or complain. Offer pictures or an interpreter. Write what the family said back, in their words, at question 3.

Result
The family knows from the first session that they lead.
Record
FRM-ECS-02 Q3

By the end of the first session (our standard)

Every contact with the family

Step 5

The practitioner

Read the family record before you see the family.

Read the priorities (question 19) and how they want information (question 9). Read the language and interpreter (question 24) and what they asked us to leave out (question 8). Read the beliefs and customs to respect (question 26). If the family record is not made yet, read REG-ECS-01 columns E and G and FRM-SUP-01 questions 7, 8 and 22. If you are covering for another practitioner, read the last contact record as well.

Result
You arrive knowing what matters to this family.
Record
None
Time limit
Before each contact (our standard)
Step 6

The practitioner

Ask the family what they want from today and what they have noticed since last time.

Ask before you tell. Let the family set the order. Ask what they have tried and what happened. A call or a message gets a shorter version of the same questions. Write what they said afterwards (step 13).

Result
The family's agenda leads, and their knowledge of their child comes first.
Record
None
Time limit
At the start of each contact (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-03, commitment 3POL-ECS-03 C3

Step 7

The practitioner

Work inside a routine the family has chosen.

Work where the routine happens: at home, at early learning or in the community. Use the child's own things, spaces and people. Do not add a separate therapy time unless the family chooses it. If a support must happen on our premises, the plan says why, the family has agreed and the Service Manager has signed it off (REG-ECS-01 columns M and AI).

Result
The strategy is practised where the child will use it.
Record
None
Time limit
At each contact (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-03, commitment 8POL-ECS-03 C8

Step 8

The practitioner

Explain what you see and why, in the way the family chose.

Use the language, format and amount the family chose at FRM-ECS-02 question 9. Use plain words and one idea at a time. Show what you mean with the child, a picture or a video, if the family likes. If you must use a technical word, explain it.

Result
The family has information they can use.
Record
None
Time limit
At each contact (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-03, commitment 7POL-ECS-03 C7

Step 9

The practitioner

Name one strength you saw.

Name a strength of the child, a parent, a carer, a brother or a sister. Say what they did. Tell the family it is worth building on. If you did not see one, ask the family what they saw.

Result
The family hears what is going well, and a strength is named at every contact.
Record
None
Time limit
At each contact (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-03, commitment 9POL-ECS-03 C9

Step 10

The practitioner

Ask the family to say or show you what they will try.

Do not ask "Do you understand?". Ask: "What will you do at bath time this week?", or ask them to show you. If the answer is unclear, say it another way. Ask the person who will do it.

Result
Any misunderstanding is found before you leave.
Record
None

Before the end of each contact (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-03, commitment 7POL-ECS-03 C7

Step 11

The practitioner

Invite each family member to take part in the way they chose.

Check FRM-ECS-02 question 7. Let each person watch, try with your help, or lead. Do not take over a task a family member wants to do. Do not push a person who wants to watch. Invite brothers, sisters and other carers where the family wants it. Say what each person's part adds.

Result
Each person takes part as they chose, and their part is seen.
Record
None
Time limit
At each contact (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-03, commitment 12POL-ECS-03 C12

Step 12

The practitioner

Agree with the family what they will try before the next contact.

Agree one or two things, no more than the family says they have time and energy for (FRM-ECS-02 question 23). Link each one to a routine. Agree how the family will tell you how it went, and when you will next be in touch.

Result
The family has a small next step that fits their week.
Record
None

Before the end of each contact (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-03, commitment 12POL-ECS-03 C12

Step 13

The practitioner

Write up the contact.

Use the session record, FRM-ECS-05 Session Record; a call or a message gets a short contact note on the same form. Write what the family asked for, said, chose and tried, and what they will try next, in their words where you can. Write the strength you named and how each person took part. Write any no, change request or difference of view, and follow step 21, 22 or 23.

Result
The record shows the family led the contact.

FRM-ECS-05

The same day (our standard)

Written on: FRM-ECS-05FRM-ECS-05

The key worker

Step 14

The key worker, or the plan lead where the family chose no key worker

Agree with the family how you will keep in touch, and what you will and will not do.

Ask how often, by what method and at what times. Say what you will do: be the family's first call; deliver most of the coaching and strategies with the family yourself, drawing on the other team members' expertise, so the family works mainly with one person; bring the team's advice to them; and bring their priorities to the team. Say what you will not do: decide for the family, or speak for them unless they ask. Add this at FRM-ECS-04 question 19, in the family's words.

Result
The family knows who to call and what to expect.
Record
FRM-ECS-04 Q19

Within 5 business days of the family's answer (our standard)

Step 15

The key worker, or the plan lead where the family chose no key worker

Start every team meeting with the family's priorities and what they want changed.

Ask the family beforehand what they want on the agenda, and whether they want to speak or be spoken for. Use FRM-ECS-02 question 19. Write the family's items first at FRM-ECS-04 question 23. Never speak for the family unless they ask.

Result
The team starts from what the family wants.
Record
FRM-ECS-04 Q23
Time limit
At every team meeting (our standard)

Step 16

Give the family the team's advice as one plain message.

Put what each member advised into one message, in the family's language and format. Say where the advice differs and give the family the choice. Do not leave the family to work out what different services mean. Send notes only to members the family agreed to at FRM-ECS-04 question 7.

Result
The family has one clear message, and the choice is theirs.
Record
FRM-ECS-04 Q27
Time limit
Within 5 business days of each team meeting (our standard)

Step 17

Ask the family whether the key worker arrangement still suits them.

Ask in the plan review conversation, together with PRO-ECS-03 step 28, so the family answers once. Ask whether it suits, and what they want to change. Where the family chose no key worker, ask whether they still want none. Ask the family, not the person beside them. The family can change it at any time (step 18). Record the next date to ask at FRM-ECS-04 question 20, and the answer in the one review record at FRM-ECS-02 question 38.

Result
The family has had the chance to change the arrangement.
Record
FRM-ECS-04 Q20; FRM-ECS-02 Q38
Time limit
At every plan review, and at least every 6 months (our standard)

Written on: FRM-ECS-04, question 12FRM-ECS-04 Q12

If the family wants a different key worker, or none:

Change the key worker as the family asks.

Say yes. Do not ask for a reason. Ask who they would like, and follow PRO-ECS-05 to find them. Add a dated line at FRM-ECS-04 question 17. If the new key worker is one of ours, they become the plan lead: update REG-ECS-01 column D and FRM-ECS-04 question 3 the same day and hand over the row. If the family chooses a key worker from another service, our plan lead stays and works to them (step 20). The outgoing key worker hands over only what the family agreed to share, so the family does not repeat their story. Supports carry on while the change happens.

Step 20

The plan lead

If the family's key worker is from another service:

Agree with the key worker how we will work with them.

Agree how we keep in touch and what we share, within the family's consent at FRM-ECS-04 question 7. Share the family record with them only as the family agreed. Our plan lead still keeps our family record and our row in REG-ECS-01, and works to the family's key worker.

Result
The family has one first call, and we work to it.
Record
FRM-ECS-04 Q18
Time limit
Within 5 business days of the family's choice (our standard)

Written on: FRM-ECS-04, question 14FRM-ECS-04 Q14

When the family wants something different

Step 21

The practitioner

If the family says no to a question, a visit, a referral, a team meeting or part of a plan:

Record the no and carry on with everything else.

Say it is the family's choice. Write the date, what they said no to and what you will do instead at FRM-ECS-02 question 8. Ask again at the next plan review. Tell the plan lead the same day. Never reduce a support because of a no.

Result
The no is respected and on record, and no support is lost.
Record
FRM-ECS-02 Q8
Time limit
The same day (our standard)

Written on: FRM-ECS-02, question 8FRM-ECS-02 Q8

Step 22

The plan lead

If the family asks to change times, place, practitioner or way of working:

Answer the request and make the change.

Tell the family whether the change can be made. If it can, make it by the date they ask. If it cannot, say why and offer the nearest option. Tell them in the way they chose. Write the request, the answer and the date done at FRM-ECS-02 question 8. If it changes the plan, change the plan with the family under PRO-ECS-08 Outcome Based Approach Procedure (Early Childhood Supports).

Result
The family's request has an answer, and the plan stays flexible.
Record
FRM-ECS-02 Q8
Time limit
Answer within 2 business days. Make the change by the date the family asks (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-03, commitment 5POL-ECS-03 C5Written on: FRM-ECS-02, question 8FRM-ECS-02 Q8

Step 23

The practitioner

If the family and a practitioner see something differently:

Record both views and agree the next step with the family.

Say what you see and why. Ask what the family sees. Do not argue or overrule. Write both at FRM-ECS-02 question 14. Agree what you will try and when you will look again. If the difference is about a child's safety, tell the child safety lead the same day and follow PRO-ECS-02.

Result
The family's view is on record and respected, and the next step is agreed.
Record
FRM-ECS-02 Q14
Time limit
The same day (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-03, commitment 3POL-ECS-03 C3Written on: FRM-ECS-02, question 14FRM-ECS-02 Q14

Step 24

Any worker

If the family is unhappy with a worker or with us:

Record it as a complaint and follow the complaints procedure.

Do not defend or explain first. Thank the family and say they will be heard. Record it on FRM-FBK-01 Feedback and Complaints Form and follow PRO-FBK-01 Feedback and Complaints Management Procedure. The family can ask for a different practitioner while it is handled. A complaint never reduces a support.

Result
The family's complaint is handled under the complaints procedure.
Record
FRM-FBK-01
Time limit
The same day (our standard)

Check the practice

Step 25

The plan lead. Where the plan lead wrote the records, another practitioner or the practice supervisor

Check the last three contact records against steps 5 to 13.

Read them at every plan review. Look for the family's agenda, a strength named, the family saying or showing what they will try, and each person taking part as they chose. Where the plan lead wrote the records, another practitioner or the reads them. Tell the practitioner what you find, and what went well, the same day. Write the gaps and what will change at FRM-ECS-02 question 43 (internal, not given to the family). A sole trader asks the practice supervisor to read their records, and the independent contact reads a sample.

Result
Gaps in the family-centred way of working are found and fixed, and are not left to chance.
Record
FRM-ECS-02 Q43
Time limit
At every plan review, and at least every 6 months (our standard)

6Decision

Decision table 1: when the family wants something different (steps 18 and 21 to 24).

IfThenStep

7If it goes wrong

IfThen
A practitioner is absent for a contactThe Service Manager arranges cover the same day, using the arrangement the family agreed (REG-ECS-01 column Y). A practitioner the family knows is first choice. The cover practitioner reads the family record before the contact (step 5). Tell the family the same day
The family wants an interpreter and none is availableMove the contact, or use a phone or video interpreter. Never use a child or a brother or sister. Write what happened at step 13
The family cannot take part in the way they choseAsk what would help. Offer a different time, place or person. Do not treat it as lack of interest

  • the family has a named plan lead and a backup, and a row in REG-ECS-01
  • the family has been told how we work, and what they said back is on record
  • each contact is written up the same day and shows the family led it
  • the family has the key worker they chose, or none, and knows who to call
  • every no, request for change, difference of view and complaint is on record and answered
  • the plan lead has checked the last three contact records at each plan review.

These records now exist:

  • the row in REG-ECS-01, with columns A, D, E and G filled
  • FRM-ECS-02 questions 3, 8 and 14
  • a session record (FRM-ECS-05) for every contact
  • FRM-ECS-02 question 43, after each plan review
  • the key worker entries in FRM-ECS-04, Section D
  • the complaint in REG-FBK-01 Complaints Register, if there was one.

docs.html:
1Purpose

The result: every has a record, made with them, of what they know and what they are good at. It also holds what is hard and what they want most. Every plan, and every new version of a plan, is checked against that record before it is signed off.

This procedure gives effect to POL-ECS-03 The Family Policy (Early Childhood Supports), C1 to C12 and C14.

2When and who

Start this procedure when:

  • a family has accepted our offer and the child's row is open in REG-ECS-01 Early Childhood Supports Register (steps 1 to 20)
  • a draft plan, or a new version of a plan, is ready for sign-off (steps 21 to 25)
  • a plan review is due, the family asks, or something changes (steps 26 to 29 and Decision table 1).

Who acts:

  • The builds the record with the family and runs the . The Service Manager names the plan lead under PRO-ECS-01 Family-Centred Practice and Key Worker Procedure.
  • The (or the plan lead themselves) drafts the plan under PRO-ECS-08 Outcome Based Approach Procedure (Early Childhood Supports), from the record. The plan lead stays accountable for it.
  • The Service Manager checks the record and the plan check before a plan is signed off.
  • The Quality Manager samples records every 3 months.
  • Every practitioner reads the record before they see the family.

In a small provider the plan lead and the Service Manager are one person. A sole trader holds every role and checks their own work at step 25. They ask the independent contact named in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register to read a sample of 3 records every 6 months.

3Before you start

  • The child's row is open in REG-ECS-01 and you are named as the plan lead.
  • You have the intake answers, FRM-SUP-01 Referral and Intake Form, questions 7, 8, 17 and 22.
  • You have the communication preferences, FRM-RGT-01 Communication, Advocacy and Support Preferences Form, if the family made one.
  • You have the family's consent on FRM-INF-01 Consent to Collect, Use and Share Information Form for anyone else you will contact.
  • You have a blank FRM-ECS-02 Family Strengths, Needs and Priorities Record.
  • You have time. Most families need two or three conversations of up to 60 minutes. The family sets the pace.
  • You do not need reports or an assessment first.

4Watch out

  • A plan written first and signed later is not the family's plan. The family stops taking part, and the plan misses what matters to them.
  • A child or a brother or sister who interprets can change what is said. The meaning is lost, and a child carries an adult's worries.
  • A family can tell you something that means a child is at . Stop and act the same day (step 5). A delay can leave a child unprotected.
  • Culture, faith and beliefs are the family's to describe. A guess from a name, a look or a language is often wrong and breaks trust.
  • Information about other adults belongs to them. Write only what the family chooses to tell you, in their words. A parent's health in a child's file can be shared by mistake.
  • A gift, payment or benefit for a referral breaks the family's trust. It can breach the duty to act with integrity, honesty and transparency (Code of Conduct Rules, s 6(1)(d)). Law changing: from 20 November 2026 the NDIS Act bans inducements to provide supports.

5Steps

Get ready

Step 1

The plan lead

Read what we already hold about the family.

Read FRM-SUP-01 questions 7, 8, 17 and 22. Read columns E, F and G of REG-ECS-01 (REG-SUP-01 Participant and Service Agreement Register, when written, will hold intake and the service agreement). Read FRM-RGT-01 if the family made one. Note what you can confirm and what is missing.

Result
You know what to confirm and what to ask, so the family is not asked twice.
Record
None
Time limit
Before each conversation with the family (our standard)
Step 2

The plan lead

Ask the family where, when and how they want to talk, and who they want there.

Offer their home, early learning, a park, our rooms, or a phone or video call. Ask about days, times, length and who will mind other children. Ask whether they want an advocate or a support person. Write the child's row number at question 1 and the answers at question 6.

Result
The conversation is at a time, place and way the family chose.
Record
FRM-ECS-02 Q1 and Q6; REG-ECS-01 col E
Time limit
Within 2 of the row being opened (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-03, commitment 1POL-ECS-03 C1Written on: FRM-ECS-02, question 1FRM-ECS-02 Q1FRM-ECS-02, question 6FRM-ECS-02 Q6

Step 3

The plan lead

Book the interpreter or communication support the family chose.

Check question 24 and FRM-SUP-01 question 8. Book for the language and dialect the family uses, in person, by phone or by video as they prefer. Book an Auslan interpreter or other support for a family member who needs one. Never use a child or a brother or sister.

Result
Everyone can speak and be understood in their own way.
Record
FRM-ECS-02 Q24
Time limit
At least 2 business days before the conversation (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-03, commitment 6POL-ECS-03 C6Written on: FRM-ECS-02, question 24FRM-ECS-02 Q24

Talk with the family

Step 4

The plan lead

Explain what the record is for and what the family controls.

Read the privacy statement in full, in the family's language and way, at the first conversation. At each later conversation remind the family that they can skip any question, stop, say no and change anything later. Say who reads the record and that the family gets a copy. Write who took part, where and in what language at question 4. Add one entry for each conversation.

Result
The family knows why we ask, who reads the answers and that they are in charge.
Record
FRM-ECS-02 Q4
Time limit
In full at the first conversation; the reminder before the first question of each later one (our standard)

Written on: FRM-ECS-02, question 4FRM-ECS-02 Q4

Step 5

The plan lead

If anything the family says, or you see, suggests a child may be at risk of harm:

Stop and tell the .

Make sure the child is safe first. Follow PRO-ECS-02 The Child Procedure (Early Childhood Supports). Do not investigate. Do not promise to keep a secret. Do not decide that it is a cultural matter. Record the concern as PRO-ECS-02 says, on FRM-ECS-01 Child Protection Concern and Report Record. The waits until the child is safe.

Result
The child safety lead has the concern and acts on it.
Record
FRM-ECS-01
Time limit
The same day (our standard)
Step 6

The plan lead

Ask who is in the family and who else the family wants in the child's life.

The family says who their family is: parents, carers, grandparents, kin, brothers and sisters, friends. Ask the best way and time to contact each person, and how the family wants each one involved. Ask whether an order or a safety concern limits contact or sharing. Write the order and where the copy is filed.

Result
The family has named their own people, and any limit is recorded before anything is shared.
Record
FRM-ECS-02 Q2; REG-ECS-01 col E
Time limit
In the first conversation (our standard)

Written on: FRM-ECS-02, question 2FRM-ECS-02 Q2

Step 7

The plan lead

Ask the family how they want to work with us.

Ask who decides what, and how the child will have a say (question 5). Ask how each adult wants to take part in their child's learning (question 7). Ask what they want left out or changed (question 8), and how they want to be given information (question 9). Where two people hold , ask each one, unless an order or the family's recorded arrangement in REG-ECS-01 column F says one person decides about supports. Never ask one to speak for the other. Check REG-ECS-01 column F and any order.

Result
The family's choices about decisions, taking part and information are written down.
Record
FRM-ECS-02 Q5, Q7, Q8 and Q9
Time limit
In the first conversation (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-03, commitment 1POL-ECS-03 C1POL-ECS-03, commitment 7POL-ECS-03 C7POL-ECS-03, commitment 12POL-ECS-03 C12Written on: FRM-ECS-02, question 5FRM-ECS-02 Q5FRM-ECS-02, question 7FRM-ECS-02 Q7FRM-ECS-02, question 8FRM-ECS-02 Q8FRM-ECS-02, question 9FRM-ECS-02 Q9and 1 more

Step 8

The plan lead

Ask what the family knows about their child, and write down their words.

Start with question 10 and listen. Then ask questions 11 to 13. They cover how the child communicates, what has been tried, and what the family sees and worries about. Ask before you say what you have seen. Do not shorten or correct their words. Enter how the child communicates in REG-ECS-01 column G.

Result
The family's knowledge comes first and is on record in their own words.
Record
FRM-ECS-02 Q10 to Q13; REG-ECS-01 col G
Time limit
Before the plan is drafted (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-03, commitment 3POL-ECS-03 C3Written on: FRM-ECS-02, question 10FRM-ECS-02 Q10FRM-ECS-02, question 11FRM-ECS-02 Q11FRM-ECS-02, question 12FRM-ECS-02 Q12FRM-ECS-02, question 13FRM-ECS-02 Q13and 1 more

Step 9

The plan lead

Ask whether the family sees anything differently from a report, an assessment or advice they have had.

Write what the document says and what the family says. Do not argue or correct. Agree with the family what you will do about the difference. A difference about a child's safety goes to the child safety lead (step 5).

Result
Both views are on record, and the family's view is respected.
Record
FRM-ECS-02 Q14
Time limit
Before the plan is drafted (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-03, commitment 3POL-ECS-03 C3Written on: FRM-ECS-02, question 14FRM-ECS-02 Q14

Step 10

The plan lead

Ask about the strengths of the child and the family, and which one to build on first.

Ask what the child is good at and loves (question 15). Ask about the strengths of each parent, carer, brother, sister and grandparent (question 16). Write the family's words. Ask which strength they want us to build on first, and how (question 17). The plan uses at least one.

Result
Strengths are on record, and the family has chosen one to build on.
Record
FRM-ECS-02 Q15 to Q17
Time limit
Before the plan is drafted (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-03, commitment 4POL-ECS-03 C4POL-ECS-03, commitment 9POL-ECS-03 C9Written on: FRM-ECS-02, question 15FRM-ECS-02 Q15FRM-ECS-02, question 16FRM-ECS-02 Q16FRM-ECS-02, question 17FRM-ECS-02 Q17

Step 11

The plan lead

Ask what is hard for the family right now.

Ask about the family's needs, not only the child's: sleep, meals, getting out, travel, money, work, other children, the parents' own wellbeing and finding services. The family can leave any of these out. Do not press.

Result
The family's needs are recorded as they describe them.
Record
FRM-ECS-02 Q18
Time limit
Before the plan is drafted (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-03, commitment 4POL-ECS-03 C4Written on: FRM-ECS-02, question 18FRM-ECS-02 Q18

Step 12

The plan lead

Ask the family to put what they want most in their own order.

Ask for up to 5 priorities for the next 6 to 12 months, for the child and the family. Write them in the family's words and read them back. The family can change the order at any time. Enter the date, who took part and the number of priorities in REG-ECS-01 column K; the priorities themselves stay on the form.

Result
The family's priorities, in their order and words, will lead the plan.
Record
FRM-ECS-02 Q19; REG-ECS-01 col K
Time limit
Before the plan is drafted (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-03, commitment 4POL-ECS-03 C4Written on: FRM-ECS-02, question 19FRM-ECS-02 Q19

Step 13

The plan lead

Ask what the family wants that therapy alone will not give.

Ask about friends, play, belonging, family time, rest and community. Say that most of a child's learning happens in daily life with the people around them. These wants go into the plan as things the family and their will do.

Result
The plan will not rest on therapy alone.
Record
FRM-ECS-02 Q20
Time limit
Before the plan is drafted (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-03, commitment 11POL-ECS-03 C11Written on: FRM-ECS-02, question 20FRM-ECS-02 Q20

Step 14

The plan lead

Ask how the child and each adult learn best, and which and times to use.

Ask how the child learns and takes part best (question 21). Ask how each parent or carer likes to learn something new (question 22). Ask for 3 to 5 routines to start with. Ask which times are off limits, and what the family can fit in between visits (question 23). Less is fine.

Result
The plan can fit the way the family learns and lives.
Record
FRM-ECS-02 Q21 to Q23
Time limit
Before the plan is drafted (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-03, commitment 5POL-ECS-03 C5POL-ECS-03, commitment 8POL-ECS-03 C8Written on: FRM-ECS-02, question 21FRM-ECS-02 Q21FRM-ECS-02, question 22FRM-ECS-02 Q22FRM-ECS-02, question 23FRM-ECS-02 Q23

Step 15

The plan lead

Ask about the family's language, culture, beliefs and community.

Ask. Never assume. Work through questions 24 to 27 in turn: languages, culture and faith, beliefs and customs, and community. Ask whether the family identifies as Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander. If they do, offer to involve a cultural contact or an Aboriginal community controlled organisation they choose. Follow POL-RGT-05 Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Cultural Safety Policy. The family can choose not to say. Write "chose not to say" and ask again at every review. Contact a community person only after the family agrees on FRM-INF-01.

Result
The family's culture and community are recorded in their words, so the plan can respect them.
Record
FRM-ECS-02 Q24 to Q27; REG-ECS-01 col G
Time limit
Before the plan is drafted (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-03, commitment 6POL-ECS-03 C6Written on: FRM-ECS-02, question 24FRM-ECS-02 Q24FRM-ECS-02, question 25FRM-ECS-02 Q25FRM-ECS-02, question 26FRM-ECS-02 Q26FRM-ECS-02, question 27FRM-ECS-02 Q27and 1 more

Step 16

The plan lead

Ask who helps the family now, and carry any link they want to FRM-ECS-03 Section G.

Ask who they turn to for help, advice or a break (question 28). Ask what help, links or contacts they want and do not yet have (question 29). Include people and informal groups, and services for the parents or other children. Carry each link the family wants to FRM-ECS-03 Everyday Routines and Participation Assessment, Section G (questions 30 and 31), which is the one home for community and service links in this module, and record at question 30 that you did. "None wanted" is an answer.

Result
The family's own network is on record, and every link they want is in its one home.
Record
FRM-ECS-02 Q28 to Q30; REG-ECS-01 col N (pointer)
Time limit
Before the plan is drafted (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-03, commitment 10POL-ECS-03 C10Written on: FRM-ECS-02, question 28FRM-ECS-02 Q28FRM-ECS-02, question 29FRM-ECS-02 Q29

Step 17

The plan lead

Read the record back to the family and fix what is missing.

Ask: "Does this sound like your family? What did we miss?" Change what the family asks you to change. Never change their own words. Write how they agreed: said, signed, or through an interpreter.

Result
The family says the record is right, or it is corrected until they do.
Record
FRM-ECS-02 Q40
Time limit
Within 5 business days of the last conversation (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-03, commitment 4POL-ECS-03 C4Written on: FRM-ECS-02, question 40FRM-ECS-02 Q40

Step 18

The plan lead

Give the family their copy of the record.

Give it in the language and form the family chose at question 9: print, large print, pictures, audio, translated, or read through with an interpreter. Ask what they want to do with it. Give a copy to anyone else only if the family agrees.

Result
The family holds their own record.
Record
FRM-ECS-02 Q41
Time limit
Within 5 business days of the read back (our standard)

Carries out: POL-ECS-03, commitment 4POL-ECS-03 C4Written on: FRM-ECS-02, question 41FRM-ECS-02 Q41

Step 19

The plan lead

Enter the record in REG-ECS-01.

Enter the family and network in column E. Enter the language, communication and culture in column G, with a pointer to the family's words on the form. The plan lead

Help the family open each link they chose, under PRO-ECS-04.

The action, owner, date and consent for each link are agreed on FRM-ECS-03 Section G under PRO-ECS-04 Inclusion Procedure (Early Childhood Supports) step 21. Offer information, an introduction, or to go along the first time. Share nothing with a service until the family has agreed on FRM-INF-01. Never accept or give a gift, payment or benefit for a referral.

Each link the family wants has an owner, a date and the family's consent.

FRM-ECS-03 Q32 and Q33; REG-ECS-01 col N and col AJ

Within 5 business days of the family naming the link, or by the date the family chooses (our standard, the same clock as PRO-ECS-04 step 21)

Make the plan theirs

Step 21

The plan lead

Give the record to the person writing the plan before the plan is drafted.

The plan starts from the priorities at question 19, the strengths, the routines and the family's culture. A plan is never drafted from reports alone. The practitioner drafting for the plan lead works under PRO-ECS-08. For an interim plan, made within 10 business days of the first session, the core questions listed in FRM-ECS-02 "What this is for" are enough; the rest are gathered across the plan period and before the first full plan.

Result
The practitioner drafting for the plan lead starts from the family's record.

None

Before the plan is drafted (our standard)
Step 22

The plan lead

Go through the draft plan with the family, one at a time.

Show where each priority from question 19 is in the plan, and whether it is in the family's words (question 32). Check that each strategy names a routine and fits how the child and the adults learn and the family's culture (question 33). Check the plan uses what the child shows they like and choose (FRM-ECS-03 question 18). Write each change the family asks for, and the date you made it. Use their language and format.

The family has seen their priorities in the plan and asked for changes.

FRM-ECS-02 Q32 and Q33

Before the plan goes for sign-off (our standard)

Ask the family whether the plan is theirs.

Ask in the family's own way: "Is this your plan?" Never hand over a signed form and ask "Do you agree?". Write how they said it: spoken, signed, through an interpreter, or through a person they chose. The answer is yes, yes after changes, no or not sure yet. Use Decision table 2.

If the family says no, or not sure yet:

Change the plan with the family and go through it again.

Ask what is not theirs. Change it, or record why it cannot change and what the family decided. Repeat steps 22 and 23. Do not send the plan for sign-off until the family says it is theirs. Supports continue as last agreed.

Within 5 business days of the family's answer (our standard)

Check the record and the plan check before signing off the plan.

For an interim plan, check that Sections A to F and questions 32 to 34 are complete; Sections G, H and J may be "in progress". For the first full plan, check that every question is answered or marked "chose not to say". Check that the answers are in the family's words, the read back and the copy are dated, the priorities in the plan match question 19, and question 34 says yes. Send it back with the reason if not. The plan lead

Review the record with the family at every plan review and whenever something changes.

Use Decision table 1. Start with question 35: what has changed. Update every answer that changed. The record matches the family's life now.

Ask the family what happened with each link.

Ask the family, not the service. The result of each service link is recorded on FRM-ECS-03 question 35 under PRO-ECS-04 step 23. Record whether it connected, is waiting, did not suit, or the family changed their mind, and what they want next. Enter the result in REG-ECS-01 column N.

Ask the family how we are doing.

If the family saysThen

7If it goes wrong

IfThen
The family does not want to answer a questionWrite "chose not to say". Go on. Ask again at the next review. It is never a reason to refuse or reduce supports
The family is tired or upset, or cannot finish in one conversationStop. Keep what is done. Book another time the family chooses
The interpreter does not come, or cannot be booked in timeMove the conversation, or use a phone or video interpreter. Never use a child or a brother or sister. Record what happened at question 4

Supports continue as last agreed
A belief, custom or practice may put the child at risk of harmDo not decide alone. Tell the child safety lead the same day. PRO-ECS-02 applies
The family asks us to leave out something the child's safety needsExplain why it cannot be left out. Record what the family said at question 8. Tell the child safety lead the same day

Work with the family on their record is finished for this version when all of these are true:

  • the family has said the record is right, and has their copy in the form they chose
  • the Service Manager has checked the record and the plan check
  • the family has said the plan is theirs, or their view is on record and the plan has not gone for sign-off
  • REG-ECS-01 shows the dates, the number of priorities and the plan check answer.

These records now exist:

  • the completed FRM-ECS-02, in the child's file
  • REG-ECS-01 columns E, G, K and N, and column X after each review
  • REG-QMS-01 entries for any change that helps other families.

  • Read the record back and fix what is missing (step 17)
  • Give the family their copy within 5 business days (step 18)
  • Go through the draft plan with the family, one priority at a time (step 22)
  • Send the plan for sign-off only when the family says it is theirs (step 23)

form.intro:
This is the for one child. It holds what the family knows about their child, and their strengths. It also holds what is hard and what they want most. It holds how they learn and live, their culture and community, and how they want to work with us. Every plan starts from it and is checked against it.

Keep one family record for each child. It is built with the family over more than one conversation. Add dated entries and never write over an old one. The family's copy is Sections A to K without question 42: questions 42 and 43 are internal checks and are not given to the family. For an interim plan under PRO-ECS-08, made within 10 of the first session, the core set is questions 2, 5, 7, 9, 10, 13, 15, 16, 18, 19, 21, 23, 24, 25 and 29; the rest are gathered across the plan period and before the first full plan. "Optional: No" in the tables means we ask the question; the family may still answer any question "chose not to say".

Who completes it:

  • The plan lead completes it with the family, at a time and place the family chooses. A parent or carer can write their own answers instead.
  • The family can bring anyone they like. An interpreter, an advocate or a cultural support person can sit in.
  • The Service Manager completes question 42 (internal, not given to the family).
  • The plan lead completes question 43 at each plan review (internal, not given to the family).

Have ready:

  • the intake answers, FRM-SUP-01 Referral and Intake Form questions 7, 8, 17 and 22, so you ask only what is missing
  • the communication preferences, FRM-RGT-01 Communication, Advocacy and Support Preferences Form, if the family made one
  • the child's row in REG-ECS-01 Early Childhood Supports Register
  • an interpreter, if the family wants one.

You do not need reports. Ask the family first. The questions are in plain words, so you can ask them aloud. Every question can be answered "chose not to say". That is a real answer and never a gap.

What happens next: PRO-ECS-03 The Family Procedure (Early Childhood Supports) sets every step. The priorities at question 19 go to FRM-ECS-03 Everyday Routines and Participation Assessment and FRM-ECS-07 Child and Family Support Plan. Community and service links the family wants are carried to FRM-ECS-03 Section G, which is their one home. The family gets a copy. The record is reviewed at every plan review and whenever something changes.
form.privacy:
This statement is for the family. Read it aloud, in the language and way the family uses.

"We ask these questions so our support fits your child and your family. You choose what to tell us. You can skip any question, stop at any time and say no to anything. Saying no does not reduce your child's supports.

We write down what you tell us, in your words. We ask about your culture, beliefs and family only so we can respect them. We write about other people in your family only what you choose to tell us.

The practitioners who work with your child read this record. So do the Service Manager and the Quality Manager. We share it with another service, such as an early learning centre, only when you agree. You choose who and what.

There is one exception. The law of [state or territory] says we must report when a child may be at . We tell you when we do, unless that would put your child at risk.

You can read this record, ask for a copy and ask us to correct it at any time. Ask [privacy contact role and contact details]. We keep this record for 7 years after your child's supports end, or until your child turns 25, whichever is later. If you are unhappy with how we handle your information you can tell us, and you can complain to the Office of the Australian Information Commissioner."

[Provider name] holds this record under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) and POL-INF-01 Information Management Policy.

form.intro:
This is the team record for one child. It names the and the key worker if the family chose one. It records what the family agreed may be shared, each team meeting and each planned move.

Keep one team record for each child. It stays open while we support the child. Add dated entries. Never write over an old entry.

Who completes it:

  • The Service Manager completes question 1, question 3 and question 41.
  • The plan lead completes the rest of Sections A to D, and Sections G and H, with the family.
  • The plan lead adds one entry to Section E for each team meeting. A key worker of ours may do it with them.
  • Every practitioner of ours adds a line to Section F each time they send or receive a document, or share with a new person.

Have these ready:

  • the child's row in REG-ECS-01 Early Childhood Supports Register
  • the family's communication preferences, on FRM-RGT-01 Communication, Advocacy and Support Preferences Form
  • nothing else for consent: Section C of this record is the family's consent record for sharing within the team
  • any court order or agency letter about who decides for the child
  • the child's plan, FRM-ECS-07 Child and Family Support Plan, once it is written.

PRO-ECS-05 Collaboration Procedure (Early Childhood Supports) sets every step. The family receives a copy of Sections A to C, of questions 13 to 15 and 17 to 20, and of every meeting entry. Question 16 stays in the file.

Do not write a child protection concern in this record. Use FRM-ECS-01 Child Protection Concern and Report Record. If you do not know an answer, write "not yet asked" and the date. Ask at the next contact with the family.
form.privacy:
This statement is for the family.

We collect this information so the people who support your child can work as one team. The NDIS Practice Standards require us to coordinate that team and to share information only with your consent.

Our practitioners who work with your child read this record. So do the Service Manager and the Quality Manager.

We share your information with a team member only as you agree at question 7. You can say no to any person or any item. Your supports continue either way.

There is one exception. The law may require us to share information without your consent to keep a child safe. PRO-ECS-02 The Child Procedure (Early Childhood Supports) sets whether and when we tell you, following the advice of the child protection agency of [state or territory].

You can ask to see this record and ask us to correct it. You can change or withdraw your consent at any time by telling [contact person]. POL-INF-01 Information Management Policy sets how we store and protect this record.
form.after:
• Plan lead: give the family a copy of Sections A to C and of questions 13 to 15 and 17 to 20 within 5 business days of the consent at question 9 (our standard).
  • Plan lead: enter the key worker, the team, the consent dates and the meeting dates in REG-ECS-01. Do it within 2 business days of each change (our standard).
  • Plan lead: send each meeting entry to the family and the team within 5 business days of the meeting (our standard).
  • Plan lead: review the team record with the family at every plan review, and at least every 6 months (our standard).
  • Service Manager: answer question 41 for each child at least every 6 months (our standard).
  • Keep the team record in the child's file for 7 years after supports end (NDIS Act 2013, section 45B, from 27 August 2026), or until the child turns 25, whichever is later (our standard).
  • Check the law of [state or territory] before a child's record is destroyed. Some laws set a longer time.

form.intro:
This is the coaching session record. It records one session in which we build the skills and confidence of a person in the child's life. It shows what the person practised in the child's routine, what they will try next, how confident they feel and what they told us.

Complete one record for each session. Question 3 sets the kind of session: coaching, joint session with another provider, capacity building support or feedback review.

When | Complete these questions

Coaching session or joint session: questions 1 to 5, 7 to 9, 14, 16 to 18 and 24 to 28 are the minimum set (24 and 27 only when they apply). Complete the rest of Sections A to G when something relevant happened or when the asks.

Capacity building support only (a guide, a video, a short training): questions 1 to 5, 7, 8, 10 and 25 to 28.

First session or feedback review: the minimum set, plus questions 12 and 19 to 23 as they apply.

Six-monthly feedback review (plan lead): Section H.

Practice supervisor's quarterly read: Section I.

Question 1 is answered once per page where several sessions for one child are recorded on one day.

Who completes it:

  • The practitioner who ran the session completes the minimum question set the same day, and the rest of Sections A to G where relevant.
  • The plan lead completes Section H at least every 6 months, at every plan review and whenever a person asks.
  • The Practice supervisor completes Section I for each record they read.

Have ready:

  • the child's plan, FRM-ECS-07 Child and Family Support Plan, for the outcomes and the routines
  • the team record, FRM-ECS-04 Team Around the Child Record, for who may take part and what may be shared
  • the last coaching session record for this child, and the last note you gave
  • the family's communication preferences, on FRM-RGT-01 Communication, Advocacy and Support Preferences Form.

Write the words of the people who took part, as they said, signed or showed them. This form is not a test of any person and it has no pass mark.

What happens next: the dates, the people coached, the ratings and the feedback go to REG-ECS-01 Early Childhood Supports Register within 2 business days. Where feedback asks for a change or a rating fell, the plan lead decides what to change within 10 business days; other feedback goes to the feedback review. PRO-ECS-06 Capacity Building Procedure (Early Childhood Supports) sets every step.
form.privacy:
Say this to the family before the first session, in the language and way they use:

"We write a record after each session. It helps us build on what you have tried, and it lets you see what we did and what you told us. We write down what you, your child, an educator or another provider say in the session, in your words where we can.

The practitioners who work with your child read this record. So do the Service Manager, the Practice supervisor and the Quality Manager when they check our work. We share it with an educator or another service only as you agreed in the team record.

You choose how far you take part. You can say no to being watched, to giving a rating, to anyone joining, or to coaching at all. Your child's supports continue either way.

We do not film, photograph or record your child unless you agree in writing first. We never film other children.

There is one exception to keeping your information private. The law may require us to share information without your consent to keep a child safe. PRO-ECS-02 The Child Procedure (Early Childhood Supports) sets whether and when we tell you, following the advice of the child protection agency of [state or territory].

You can read this record, ask us to correct it and tell us if you are unhappy with anything. Ask [privacy contact role and contact details]."

Tell an educator or another provider that the family can read what they say.

[Provider name] handles this record under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) and POL-INF-01 Information Management Policy.
form.after:
• Practitioner: complete this record the same day (our standard).
  • Plan lead: enter the date, the people coached, the end rating and the feedback in REG-ECS-01 columns W and X within 2 business days, from the signed record (our standard).
  • Plan lead: decide what to change within 10 business days of the session (our standard). Tell the person who gave the feedback within 5 business days of the decision (our standard).
  • Plan lead: complete Section H at least every 6 months and at every plan review (our standard).
  • Practice supervisor: read 2 records for each practitioner every 3 months (our standard).
  • A person with can ask for a copy of any record about their child. We give it within 10 business days (our standard).
  • The record is filed in the child's file. Keep it for 7 years after supports end (NDIS Act 2013, section 45B, from 27 August 2026), or until the child turns 25, whichever is later (our standard). Check the law of [state or territory] before a child's record is destroyed. Some laws set a longer time.

form.intro:
This is the support plan for one child and their family. It says what will change in the child's and the family's daily life. It also says what each person will do to help, and how we will know it is working. The family keeps a copy. Every worker who sees the child follows it.

The plan is made of . Each one is something the child or the family will do in a routine, a place and with people, which anyone could see or hear. Each outcome has supports, which the Quality Indicators call interventions, and a way of measuring.

Keep one plan for each child. Version 0 is the interim plan: one to three starting outcomes and their supports, agreed with the family within 10 business days of the first session, with no five-level scale and no Service Manager approval. starts under it. Version 1 is the first full plan and replaces it. A new version is made whenever an outcome, a measure or a support changes. The last approved version stays in force until the new one is approved.

Who completes it:

  • The completes every section except Section B and questions 24 and 25, with the family, at a time and place the family chooses. Where the plan lead asks a practitioner to write a part, the plan lead stays accountable.
  • A parent or carer can write their own answers instead. The family can bring anyone: an interpreter, an advocate or a cultural support person.
  • The practitioner who assesses the child completes Section B. For FRM-ECS-03 that is the plan lead.
  • The Service Manager completes questions 24 and 25.

Have ready:

  • the , FRM-ECS-02 Family Strengths, Needs and Priorities Record
  • the assessment, FRM-ECS-03 Everyday Routines and Participation Assessment, and any other assessment report
  • the team record, FRM-ECS-04 Team Around the Child Record, for who may see what
  • the family's communication preferences, on FRM-RGT-01 Communication, Advocacy and Support Preferences Form
  • the child's row in REG-ECS-01 Early Childhood Supports Register
  • for a check or review, the last approved version and the FRM-ECS-05 Coaching Session Record entries for the plan period
  • an interpreter, if the family wants one.

Where the provider has adopted PRO-SUP-02 Support Planning Procedure and FRM-SUP-02 Participant Support Plan Template, this plan is the child's support plan under them, and the FRM-SUP-02 sections that hold the critical summary, consent, risks, emergencies and who has the plan are attached; where FRM-SUP-02 asks what this plan also asks, answer it here and write "see FRM-ECS-07 question" and its number there. Until a Rise version exists, question 18 holds the critical information, emergency steps, risks and who holds the plan. This plan does not authorise any restraint, seclusion or other restrictive practice.

What happens next: PRO-ECS-08 Outcome Based Approach Procedure (Early Childhood Supports) sets every step. The family gets their copy within 5 business days of approval: the page "Our plan in our words" at the end of this form, one page per outcome, in the language and format they chose. We check each outcome with the family every 3 months and review the plan at least every 6 months.
form.privacy:
This statement is for the family. Read it aloud, in the language and way the family uses.

"We write this plan with you. It says what you want for your child and your family, what each of us will do, and how we will know it is working. We use your words where we can.

You choose what goes in the plan. You can say no to any question and to any part of the plan. Saying no does not reduce your child's supports.

The workers who support your child read this plan. So do the Service Manager and the Quality Manager. We give the plan to a teacher, an educator or another service only if you agree, and only the parts you agree to.

We write down how your child is going and use it to show you. We do not use it to judge you or your family.

There is one exception. The law may require us to share information without your consent to keep a child safe. PRO-ECS-02 The Child Procedure (Early Childhood Supports) sets whether and when we tell you, following the advice of the child protection agency of [state or territory].

You can read this plan, ask for a copy in the way that suits you, and ask us to correct it at any time. Ask [privacy contact role and contact details]."

Tell an educator or another provider who adds to this plan that the family will read what they say.

[Provider name] holds this plan under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) and POL-INF-01 Information Management Policy.
form.after:
• Service Manager: approve the plan, or return it with the reasons, within 5 business days of the family agreeing (step 16, our standard). The interim plan (version 0) needs no approval.
  • Plan lead: enter the approved plan in REG-ECS-01 within 2 business days of approval (step 17, our standard).
  • Plan lead: give the family their copy within 5 business days of approval. Ask them to say it back (steps 18 and 19, our standard).
  • Plan lead: give the plan to each of our workers who sees the child before their next contact (step 20, our standard).
  • Plan lead: hold a progress check at least every 3 months. Enter it in REG-ECS-01 within 2 business days (steps 22 and 24, our standard).
  • Plan lead: give the family a progress report at each plan review, and at least every 6 months (step 25, our standard).
  • A person with parental responsibility can ask for a copy of any record about their child. We give it within 10 business days (our standard).
  • The plan is filed in the child's file. Keep it for 7 years after supports end (NDIS Act 2013, section 45B, from 27 August 2026), or until the child turns 25, whichever is later (our standard). Check the law of [state or territory] before a child's record is destroyed. Some laws set a longer time.

register.proves:
This register holds one row for every child who receives from [Provider name]. The row is the index to the child's file. It shows who the is, who is in the team, what the family agreed to, and when each plan, review and report was due and done.

  • Indicators evidenced: s 56 (1) to s 56 (4), s 56 (5)(a) and s 56 (5)(b).
  • Also s 57 (1) to s 57 (8), on the family.
  • Also s 58 (1) to s 58 (4), on inclusion, and s 59 (1) to s 59 (4), on collaboration.
  • Also s 60 (1) to s 60 (5), on capacity building, and s 61 (2), on practitioner skills.
  • Also s 62 (1) to s 62 (6), on outcomes.
  • Legal basis: National Disability Insurance Scheme (Provider Registration and Practice Standards) Rules 2018, Schedule 5, clauses 3 to 9. Section 20(3), item 18 of those Rules applies Schedules 1 and 5 to early intervention supports for early childhood.
  • No NDIS instrument sets the columns of this register. The columns are our standard, built from the indicators.
  • Each fact is held once. The forms hold the detail and the family's words. This register holds the dates, the names, the counts, the record numbers and a one-line pointer to the form.
  • Clearances and training are in REG-HRM-01 Worker Screening Register and REG-HRM-02 Training and Competency Register. Intake and the service agreement are in REG-SUP-01 Participant and Service Agreement Register (Rise version not yet written); until it exists, column F holds who has .
  • Retention: keep each row for 7 years after supports end, or until the child turns 25, whichever is later (our standard; NDIS Act 2013, section 45B (from 27 August 2026): records of claims and supports are kept for 7 years).
  • Retention where column J holds a record number: keep the row for 45 years (Royal Commission into Institutional Responses to Child Sexual Abuse, recommendation 8.1; our standard). Check the child safe and records law of [state or territory] at adoption and before any row is destroyed.

Columns A to G and I are filled before the first session, and columns H and Y by the end of it. Column J stays blank until a record exists. Columns K to X and AH are filled as the plan is made and followed. Columns Z, AA and AD are filled when an interruption, a transition or an exit comes up. Columns AB, AC, AE, AF, AG, AI, AJ, AK and AL are kept current for every row.
register.entry:
1. The opens the row within 2 of the family accepting our offer (our standard). The Service Manager names the plan lead that day.
  2. Use one row for each child. Brothers and sisters each get their own row, linked in column AF.
  3. Fill columns A to G and I before the first session. Column J stays blank until a record exists. The first session does not go ahead while column I is empty for the type of setting it is in.
  4. Fill columns H and Y by the end of the first session.
  5. Fill every other column within 2 business days of the form or meeting that produces it (our standard).
  6. Write "not yet asked" with a date when a required answer is not known. Ask at the next contact with the family.
  7. Never overwrite or delete an entry. A correction is a new version of the row, with the date, your name and the reason.
  8. Columns H, N, R, X, Z, AH, AI, AJ and AK hold dated entries. Add each new entry underneath the last one. Column AL holds one date, replaced at each check.
  9. The family's own words stay in the forms (FRM-ECS-02, FRM-ECS-03, FRM-ECS-05). This register holds dates, names, counts, record numbers and one-line pointers. Where a short phrase of the family's is entered, such as "none wanted" in column N, it is entered as it was said, signed or shown. Nobody tidies it.
  10. Column J takes record numbers only. Never write what was seen, said or suspected in this register.
  11. When the plan lead is away for more than 5 business days, the Service Manager names another worker to keep the row.
  12. When the system is down, complete the paper forms. Enter the row within 1 business day of the system coming back.
  13. A sole trader is the plan lead and keeps every row.

A row is closed only when all of these are true:

  • column AD is filled and column AC says "exited"
  • the family has their final progress report and their copy of the last plan
  • column AA shows the handover was given, or the family's decision that none was wanted
  • every consent line in column Q has a withdrawn date or an end date
  • nothing in column AE, AI, AJ, AK or AL is still due.

register.see:
• The plan lead and the key worker can see the rows of the children they work with.
  • The Service Manager, the Quality Manager and the Chief Executive can see every row.
  • A worker can see columns B, E, G, M, P, S, U and Y for the children they see. They cannot browse the register.
  • Column J shows record numbers only. Only the child safety lead, the deputy and the Chief Executive can open the forms behind those numbers.
  • A person with parental responsibility can ask to see their child's row and ask us to correct it. We answer within 10 business days (our standard).
  • Before a row is released, the child safety lead checks columns E and J. Nothing is released that an order forbids or that could put the child at risk.
  • Another provider in the team receives only what column Q allows.
  • An auditor or the NDIS Commission sees rows only as the law allows or requires.

Rows hold sensitive personal and health information about children. Keep the register in [system name], with a login for each person and a log of changes. Lock away any paper form.

POL-INF-01 Information Management Policy sets the wider privacy rules.
register.rows: The rows are the data. They are kept in the workbook or system built to this specification, not in this document. Where a cell would otherwise hold a list (columns E, H, I, M, N, P, Q, R, V, X, Z, AB, AH, AI, AJ and AK), a second sheet holds one row per entry, keyed to the child's record number in column A.
